news.title: AI在信用社合并中能做什么、不能做什么
news.snippet: AI可辅助premerger分析，但合并成功仍依赖文化整合与人工决策。
news.raw_snippet:
Premerger Analysis

AI can support premerger analysis as well by gathering research, organizing financial information and identifying questions leaders may not have considered. McHenry said institutions can use it to conduct a red-team-style assessment that challenges the proposed transaction and highlights risks, but it should not determine whether a merger proceeds. [...] McHenry said the strategic objective behind a merger must remain the primary filter for every integration decision, regardless of whether AI is involved. The technology becomes most useful when teams are attempting to assemble, organize and compare large amounts of information from the two institutions. [...] “AI can be a force multiplier for the different work streams and the different teams because it can help do what humans can do, but do it much faster,” McHenry said.

# AI companies are desperate for cash and don’t know where it will come from

The companies have been borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars, selling fresh stock and cooking up more novel and potentially risky new methods of financing.

7 min

(Washington Post illustration; iStock/TWP)

By Shira Ovide

The biggest bet in the history of the United States keeps getting bigger and we’re all hanging on for the ride. [...] Technology companies recently launched a record scramble for cash to pay for data centers, computer chips and technology and equipment to power artificial intelligence. This boom is so expensive that even Silicon Valley giants are bleeding cash and companies are now racing one another to collect or borrow other people’s money for the estimated $10 trillion of AI-related spending in coming years.

news.title: “雇用机器人，解雇人类”：比尔·盖茨的警告与微软买断
news.snippet: 盖茨曾警示自动化冲击就业，微软推出自愿离职方案以适应AI转型。
news.raw_snippet:
"The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We'll learn from it," Microsoft's chief people officer Amy Coleman said in a memo to staff.  
Microsoft says AI is not behind the move. Reuters, however, reports the company is looking to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments. [...] ## Gates' Warning

Bill Gates calls the AI age an "evolutionary event," where humans are no longer the smartest things on the planet. He expects AI to take over almost all work skills, starting with white-collar jobs, followed by blue collar jobs and physical labour. [...] For advanced economies, the IMF said helping workers move into new roles and protecting those hit hardest should be policy priorities.

Gates's warning and Microsoft's buyout offer are separate events, but it's almost impossible to ignore that they hit on back-to-back days.

As companies increasingly invest money into AI, who bears the cost of the shift is the big question the answer at this point.
